claims.text: The compared Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets are equiatomic, thermomechanically processed, and single-phase FCC.
Omitting one or more elements from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni disrupts local short-range chemical order.
Omitting specific elements from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni changes local lattice distortions.
Short-range chemical order and local lattice distortions modify the stacking-fault-energy distribution.
Local lattice distortions alter dislocation pinning effectiveness.
Differences in constituent-atom lattice parameters hinder partial-dislocation motion in CoNiCrFeMn nanowires through friction.
Hindering partial-dislocation motion produces hardening and reduced ductility in CoNiCrFeMn nanowires.
Changes in stacking-fault energy and dislocation pinning alter the activation and mobility of dislocations.
Changes in stacking-fault energy and dislocation pinning alter the ease of slip and deformation-twin formation.
The local structural changes caused by element omission lead to differences in strain hardening and failure behavior between the quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit measurable differences in dislocation mobility and dislocation-density evolution.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit measurable differences in stacking-fault and twin formation.
The omitted element or elements can either reduce or enhance dislocation pinning.
Changes in dislocation pinning caused by element omission produce altered strain-hardening rates and failure modes.
Atom-probe tomography can quantify the proposed short-range chemical ordering.
Atom-probe tomography can quantify local stacking-fault-energy variations.
